gaps.quote: Both procedures come from one fixed linear network
gaps.note: The page asserts that the interchange and the butterfly layers both come from one network but never shows how the network's roles and child calls produce either procedure.

gaps.quote: The $n\log n$ cost scans all $V$ stored bits at each of the $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels
gaps.note: The bound O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) needs the stored bit volume V to be O(n), but the page never states or derives that V is proportional to n.

gaps.term: u and d as powers of lg n
gaps.quote: Here $u$ and $d$ are powers of $\lg n$ with exponents below one.
gaps.note: This is asserted as a fact with no argument on the page, and the reader cannot check that the field width and the number of selected chunks are powers of lg n.

gaps.quote: The logarithmic factor drops by the fixed power $\kappa$ because $\kappa$ is set by the smallest margin in the sources' cost table.
gaps.note: The page does not explain how the rows of the sources' cost table are related to the machine's running time, so the step from the margins to the total bound cannot be checked from the page.
The page says the splitting, gates and reassembly cost O(1) per unit volume, which gives O(1), not the O(e^tau+1) term used; the source of the e^tau term and the base case F(1)=O(1) are not given.

The page says e changes meaning but gives no new meaning, so later uses of e (a field of e digits, e at most d, O(e^lambda)) cannot be checked; a field is said to have e/m digits in the previous sentence but e digits here.
